facts.statement: The genus Ignotosaurus was described by Martínez and colleagues in 2013.
The type species of the genus is Ignotosaurus fragilis.
Ignotosaurus lived during the Late Triassic (Carnian) in northwestern Argentina alongside early dinosaurs like Herrerasaurus.
facts.quote: It was therefore contemporary with early dinosaurs such as Herrerasaurus, and lived in the same place.

facts.statement: The name Ignotosaurus means 'unknown lizard' because only a single right ilium fossil is known.
facts.quote: The name, meaning 'unknown lizard' from the Latin 'ignotus' 'unknown' and the Greek 'σαυρος' 'lizard', is quite apt as there is only one specimen known and this specimen is only known from the right ilium.

facts.statement: The known fossil is an ilium approximately 70 mm long, making the total size of the animal difficult to determine accurately.
facts.quote: This ilium is approximately 70 mm long, but it is difficult to say accurately how large Ignotosaurus was.

facts.statement: The specific name 'fragilis' refers to the ilium's blade, which has a central portion only 1 mm thick.
facts.quote: The ilium is slender, and its blade has an extremely thin central portion (only 1 mm thick), hence the specific name 'fragilis'.

facts.statement: The ilium has a saddle-shaped lateral profile and is longer than it is deep.
facts.quote: It has the saddle-shaped lateral profile of most silesaurids, and is longer than it is deep.

facts.statement: The supraacetabular crest is laterally oriented and helps form the socket for the femur.
facts.quote: The supraacetabular crest is laterally oriented and forms part of the articulation for the femur.

facts.statement: The preacetabular process is angled at 90 degrees to the iliac blade and points anterolaterally, serving as a diagnostic feature of the species.
facts.quote: The preacteabular process is flattened anteroposteriorly and is angled at 90° to the iliac blade, pointing anterolaterally - these are the diagnostic features of this species.

facts.statement: Ignotosaurus is thought to be closely related to Silesaurus, Sacisaurus, and Eucoelophysis, though this is uncertain due to limited fossil evidence.
facts.quote: Ignotosaurus is thought to be most closely related to Silesaurus, Sacisaurus and Eucoelophysis, but as only one of the three characteristic features for silesaurids is preserved this is not certain

facts.statement: Ignotosaurus was likely a herbivore that competed for food with rhynchosaurs, cynodonts, and early dinosaurs in river basin habitats.
facts.quote: As Ignotosaurus was probably a herbivore, like other silesaurids, it would probably have flourished here, competing for food with rhynchosaurs, cynodonts and possibly some early dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Ignotosaurus belongs to the family Silesauridae.
Ignotosaurus is classified within the unranked group Dinosauriformes.
Ignotosaurus lived between 237 and 227.3 million years ago during the Carnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)
